title: How big is four thirds times four?
description: Four thirds is multiplied by four, and the product is placed on a number line next to both numbers. When both numbers are greater than one, the product lands beyond both. Keeko raises the doubt of putting the four under the line as well.
teaching_notes: One idea: when both numbers are greater than one, the product is greater than both of them. Watch for students who write a whole number under the line, which shrinks the product.

source: Multiply 4/3 × 4 and compare the product with both numbers.
video_script.why: A learner sees that a product of two numbers greater than one is greater than both of them.
video_script.substitution: the numbers of the book's own first situation, four thirds and four
video_script.anchor: a number line with the numbers four thirds and four marked, and one marked as a reference
video_script.wrong_move: writes the whole number four under the line as well as over it
video_script.payoff_line: Four thirds times four is sixteen thirds, which is greater than both numbers

final_answer.spoken: sixteen thirds, which is greater than both numbers

video_script.fraction_reading: four thirds, sixteen thirds, four twelfths
maths_rules: 4/3 is greater than 1 because 4 is more than 3
5 1/3 is greater than 1 1/3 and greater than 4
the slip: 4/(3 × 4) = 4/12, which is less than both numbers
video_script.design: A number line with one marked, the two numbers placed on it, and the product landing beyond both.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; the numbers 4/3 and 4 with a times sign between them

marks.pose: the two numbers arrive with a times sign between them
marks.ask: a question mark glows beside the product

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about the size of a product.
<bookmark mark='pose'/>Multiply four thirds by four, and compare the product with both numbers.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Is the product smaller or greater than the two numbers?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a number line from 0 to 6 with 1 marked in the accent colour; the stretch from 0 to 1 and the stretch beyond 1 are shaded differently

marks.sort: the number line arrives with one marked

narration: <bookmark mark='sort'/>The size of a product depends on where each number sits.
<bookmark mark='zero'/>A number is either between zero and one, or greater than one.
<bookmark mark='whole'/>A whole number can be written as a fraction with one below it.

marks.given: the two numbers are written under the word Given

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the numbers are four thirds and four.

beats.on_screen: To find: 4/3 × 4, and how it compares with 4/3 and 4

marks.find: the words To find and the product are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to multiply them and compare the product with both numbers.

marks.cmp: each number is placed against the mark for one on the number line

narration: <bookmark mark='cmp'/>Step one, compare each number with one, because that decides how the product behaves.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Four thirds has a top that is more than its bottom, so it is greater than one.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Four is greater than one too.

marks.mult: the four is rewritten as four over one
marks.tb: the tops and the bottoms are multiplied in pairs

narration: <bookmark mark='mult'/>Step two, write four as four over one, and multiply the tops and the bottoms.
<bookmark mark='tb'/>That is four times four on top, and three times one below.

beats.on_screen: the product as 5 1/3 on the number line; 5 1/3 > 1 1/3 and 5 1/3 > 4

marks.cmp2: the product lands on the number line as five and one third
marks.big: arrows show it is beyond one and one third
marks.also: an arrow shows it is beyond four

beats.moves_through: the product slides along the number line
narration: <bookmark mark='cmp2'/>Step three, compare the product with each number. Sixteen thirds is the same as five and one third.
<bookmark mark='big'/>Five and one third is greater than four thirds, which is one and one third.
<bookmark mark='also'/>It is also greater than four.

marks.why: both numbers are marked as greater than one

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Four thirds times four is sixteen thirds, which is greater than both numbers.
<bookmark mark='why'/>Both numbers are greater than one, so each makes the other grow.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: 4/3 × 4 = 4/12 appears and is struck through; the four is rewritten as 4/1

marks.doubt: Keeko's bubble shows the four under the line as well
marks.slip: the product is shown smaller than both numbers
marks.fix: the four is rewritten as four over one

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the four goes under the line as well, so the product is four twelfths.
<bookmark mark='slip'/>Four twelfths is smaller than both numbers, which cannot be right.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>A whole number goes over one, and the one stays below.
Four thirds and four are both greater than one, so the product has to grow.
